You have to distinguish between paid shills and unpaid ones.

The problem is identifying a paid shill from someone who just legitimately disagrees with you. And when you just start accusing anyone you disagree with as being a shill the whole discussion spirals out of control.

There are ways of at least beginning to sort them out. First of all for anyone to be a paid shill there has to be someone to pay. This means basically governments, large corporations and political parties. The constant brigading that goes back and forth on the 'political' subs on reddit are probably entirely self-identified crusaders rather than shills. A second way is to check back through comment history. If, for instance, defending Monsanto comes up time after time on different posts for weeks and months then it is very likely that said person is being paid. There are other signs to look for as well.

How do you know the guy isn't just a die hard Monsanto fan that defends them every chance he gets? Some people do that kind of thing for free.

I, for example, always argue that NATO has no business fucking with Russia. I heard a very convincing Dan Carlin podcast about the issue and I wholeheartedly agree with him. If you went through my reddit history you'd find all sorts of comments to that point. Would that make you think I'm a shill on the Kremlin payroll? I'm not, I can promise you that. My local bar doesn't accept rubles.

There are more than a few clues. To begin with examine the post history. Look to see if 'Monsanto' or 'glyphosate' keeps coming up time after time for weeks or months on end. Then look at the suspect's general interests to see if there is any other contributing 'crusade' that might explain the continued focus. Also check the number of different 'subs' or 'verses' or whatever that the suspect comments on dear old Monsanto in. If there is a vast number it indicates 'searching' for the keyword. If the suspect rarely or never comments on other subjects in said subs then it is definite proof of searching for Monsanto the name. Then there is the level of knowledge about the subject. A plethora of false statements and an index of interest in other matters non-technical heightens the suspicion. Monsanto does not put its chemists to work blundering about social media. Quite often you will find that those you suspect of being paid haven't even read Monsanto's own official propaganda. One statement I remember is the nonsense that 'Monsanto doesn't sue farmers'. This is easy for me as I personally know two who have been sued, AND Monsanto's own official statements make mention of about 147 cases (in the US leaving aside what is often low grade thuggery elsewhere). The people who Monsanto or its PR firms hire for this are basically internet demons in need of spare change. There is a word that describes these people when the subject is China. The word is " wu - Mao". No connection to Mao. It is Pinyin for "50 cents", the going rate per post for pro-CPC posts.

OK, back to the crusades. If you find no evidence that the commentator is spending his efforts as part of a wider campaign, say 'fighting anti-science', opposing what they think the 'liberals' are spreading, generally being St. George for the oppressed corporate class, etc. then you've pretty well found a paid advocate. The internet draws all sorts of crazy people, but I have yet to encounter any evidence that anyone has fallen so deeply in love with any corporation that they are willing to spend their time in unrequited acts of love for their obsession. If one or two such people exist then they may be one or two amongst the many defenders that spring up every time Monsanto is mentioned. Not to dismiss entirely the fact that one real person may have 20 different internet names.

So that's how you do it. Look at the wider picture. As to Russia the first thing to note is that the subject is much, much, much bigger than an individual corporation. It draws people with all sorts of different opinions, not stray nuts who are in love with a corporation. To distinguish a 'Putin-shill' from others you have to have a certain knowledge about the general opinions of various political persuasions and also have some knowledge of Russian culture and the way things are done in Russia. The Russian government actually has a whole building full of them, and I remember an amusing thing I read in a Russian news outlet some time ago. The social media employees of the government were pleased as punch. They had been moved from their old office which was cramped and falling apart into bright new quarters. Typically Russian. The Chinese do things quite differently, and suspect the American government does so also.
